## ⛔ Closing as **superseded** — residue is **0 of 5**, not 6. The dispatch was burned by a duplicate split, not a stale count.

Dispatched, and the dev correctly refused to produce a PR. Re-derived on `origin/main` @ `a718ee3dd`: **every one of this card's five in-scope sites already reads `v16`** — `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md:1934`, `action-params.zod.ts:376` and `:409`, `migrations/registry.ts:1557`, `entries/semantic/17.action-session-roles-to-positions.ts:23` — and so do the three regenerated artifacts this card said were carrying a published wrong version.

They were delivered by **#10079** (spec surface, PR #10252) and **#10080** (governed skills surface, PR #10180), both closed-completed.

### ⭐ The actual cause, and it is worth acting on

This card was filed **2026-08-19**, carving #9872's residue into Split A (skills) + Split B (spec). The **2026-08-20** triage on #9872 then carved *the same residue again* into #10079 (spec) + #10080 (skills) + a narrowed #9872, **without referencing #9991 — which already existed and already owned that exact scope.** #10079 and #10080 were dispatched, delivered and closed; this card stayed open and got dispatched today against work that had already shipped.

⇒ **The duplicate split burned the dispatch, not a stale count.** ⚠️ Worth a look at whether the triage step reads a card's existing open follow-ons before splitting its residue — recorded here rather than filed, since it is a process observation about a lane that is not mine to card.

### ⛔ #9872 is NOT closable, and there is a live contradiction only the maintainer can settle

Two rulings disagree about the same five remaining lines:

| ruling | date | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **#9991's own body** | 2026-08-19 | *"Ruled: they stay as they are … Editing them would be changing evidence to match prose."* |
| **#9872 triage comment** | 2026-08-20 | *"this re-grade is the explicit yes: they are in scope for the next dispatch of this card."* |

⭐ The dev's recommendation is **C — split the two groups**, and the distinction is *whose voice the text is in*, which is why neither blanket ruling fits:

- The four `check-org-identifier.mjs` fixture lines (`:597`, `:601`, `:603`, `:641`) are **quoted specimens of author text** — the corpus exists to prove the detector does not flag documentation. Rewriting a specimen to `v16` makes it a specimen of a sentence no author ever wrote, degrading its fidelity while moving zero expected counts. ⇒ Keep.
- `audit-writers.test.ts:1653` is **the repo speaking in its own voice**, and it renders the wrong date into CI output for whoever reads a failing run. Verified nothing pins it: the title string occurs exactly once tree-wide and `plugin-audit` has no snapshot files. ⇒ One word, risk-free.

⛔ Not my ruling to make on someone else's card — recording it so #9872's next dispatch starts from the split rather than from two contradicting blanket rulings.

### ⚠️ A tooling finding every seat should have

The dev's mandated read-back appeared to show the report marker **stripped**, and it was not: the MCP `issue_read get_comments` view returns bodies with HTML comments removed and the rest HTML-escaped, so a faithful comment renders as a mangled one. Fetching the same comment raw over REST shows the marker intact at byte 0. ⇒ **The MCP comment view is not byte-faithful and must not be used as a read-back instrument** — otherwise a dev "repairs" a comment that was never broken and posts its report twice. (I have seen exactly that double-post happen tonight.)

Closing. ⛔ Nothing was edited; the placeholder branch `claude/issue-9991-tenantid-v11-residue` is 0 commits ahead and safe to delete.
